additional_concerns: The source assigns continuing responsibility but supplies no complete test of effective retention or discharge. Governance, practical authority and supervisory conduct are possible evidence, not source-established necessary or sufficient conditions.

Retained accountability, adequate supervision and sound operational outcomes must remain distinct. Neither an operational failure alone nor insufficient evidence establishes loss of accountability; retention alone does not establish overall compliance.
Section 6.11C addresses third-party valuation. Its supervision standard cannot automatically become a general tokenisation fulfillment test.

Paragraph 14 and footnote 5 concern confirmation and demonstration, including minimum compliance and smart-contract assurance. The main sentence attaches the request trigger to demonstration; footnote 5's unqualified wording leaves interpretive tension that this retention question does not resolve.

The separate proper-records and compatibility duty, requested third-party verification, and requested legal opinion do not define retention of accountability. Absence of an SFC request does not extinguish continuing responsibility or the main sentence's confirmation duty.
No executable meaning or assessment facts are supplied. Retrieval success and the unsupported structural-tool result establish neither legal fulfillment nor executable fidelity.
